name: The New Pornographers
label: Matador
lede: A Vancouver side project built from a grunge-pop songwriter, a country singer, a cryptic poet and a filmmaker on keyboards turned into the most crowded, most hook-stuffed power-pop band of the century, and stayed together for thirty years because nobody ever had to choose.

eras.title: A side project that took three years
eras.text: Carl Newman had fronted Vancouver's Zumpano; Dan Bejar had just started Destroyer; Neko Case had a country career of her own. The New Pornographers were meant as a side project for all of them, and the first album took nearly three years to finish.

years.h: Carl Newman starts a Vancouver collective
years.p: [[A.C. Newman|bb40af12-0dfd-4a53-bfe1-666a9e49dfb2]] gathers [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]], [[Dan Bejar|9f142b12-570e-464d-9cb0-f1d579bb6a66]] of [[Destroyer|61604b45-8a91-4e33-a1b6-45d7b1fec4e5]], bassist [[John Collins|17fe13d1-ca12-4e28-a7d5-0deb9f631650]] and filmmaker [[Blaine Thurier|57ec12b3-f6ae-4cb1-bdb2-d53c168adf08]] on keyboards, with Fisher Rose on drums.
years.xp: Newman came out of the Vancouver bands Superconductor and [[Zumpano|52203489-c14f-4e60-8aa4-4691da1c974f]]. He took the name from a Japanese film, The Pornographers, and it doubled as a nod to the 1970s pop group the New Seekers and to The Pornographers, a song on Destroyer's debut We'll Build Them a Golden Bridge.

years.h: Kurt Dahle of Limblifter takes over the drums
years.p: [[Kurt Dahle|8ebf990e-845f-4abf-a606-1f6cf14f2c23]], from Vancouver's [[Limblifter|b8558bc4-a8f9-4abe-9b27-aa4c796c08fb]] and The Age of Electric, replaces Fisher Rose behind the kit.

years.h: Mass Romantic on Mint Records
years.p: Vancouver's Mint Records releases the debut, produced by David Carswell and John Collins. Entertainment Weekly calls it a perfect pop album.
years.xp:
Newman and Bejar split the songwriting, and Bejar's Breakin' the Law was a Destroyer song first. The closing chorus is credited to the Camp Northstar Kids' Chorus, a joke on the film Meatballs: it's just the band singing.

Letter from an Occupant, sung by Neko Case, became the only single, in April 2002.

eras.title: The critics' secret goes to Matador
eras.text: Mass Romantic didn't chart anywhere, but it won a Juno and topped critics' lists, and the band's first tour sold out despite blown voices and broken gear. The second album was the first on Matador in America.

years.h: Mass Romantic wins the Juno for Alternative Album
years.p: The album that never charted in Canada or the US wins the Juno Award for Alternative Album of the Year. Pitchfork had ranked it No. 9 of 2001.

years.h: A Western Canada tour, filmed for Better Off in Bed
years.p: Director Reginald Harkema films the band's 2002 Western Canada tour for the documentary Better Off in Bed.

years.h: Electric Version, the first on Matador
years.p: Mint in Canada and Matador in the US release the second album. Rolling Stone later puts it at No. 79 among the 100 best albums of the 2000s.

years.h: Todd Fancey joins on guitar
years.p: [[Todd Fancey|5f1c3469-cbed-4606-b656-a1cd30b2571c]], also a solo artist, joins as guitarist and backing vocalist.

years.h: The band blocks its own documentary, Better Off in Bed
years.p: Reginald Harkema's tour film Better Off in Bed plays film festivals, but according to Wikipedia the band disliked how it was portrayed and stepped in to stop a wider release.

eras.title: Twin Cinema and a niece on keyboards
eras.text: The New Pornographers peaked commercially while their members' solo careers took off too. Neko Case's schedule got too full for touring, and the fix turned out to be family: a young Victoria singer who happened to be Newman's niece.

years.h: Kathryn Calder, Carl Newman's niece, joins
years.p: [[Kathryn Calder|aeb6221d-f90d-4f45-a36a-eccd09b749fd]] of [[Immaculate Machine|9f01b9ea-162d-47f5-93b1-3f6a3aeb4b24]] starts filling in for Neko Case on tour and becomes a full member.
years.xp: Calder's mother was adopted as a baby and later found her birth family, which included Carl Newman. Calder learned he was her uncle as a teenager, while she was already playing in a band.

years.h: Twin Cinema reaches No. 44 in America
years.p: Released by Mint and Matador, Twin Cinema gets a 9.0 from Pitchfork and is PopMatters' album of 2005. By 2010 it had sold 138,000 copies in the US.

years.h: Neko Case's Fox Confessor debuts at No. 54
years.p: [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]]'s solo album Fox Confessor Brings the Flood debuts at No. 54 on the Billboard 200. Her 2009 album Middle Cyclone will reach No. 3.

years.h: Challengers, recorded in Brooklyn
years.p: Made at the Seaside Lounge in Brooklyn and released by Matador, Challengers debuts at No. 34. Kathryn Calder sings her first lead, Failsafe.

years.h: Together, dedicated to Kathryn Calder's mother
years.p: Released by Matador, Together reaches No. 18 in the US. It's dedicated to Calder's mother, who died of ALS while Calder cared for her.

eras.title: The best chart spot, a new drummer, one fewer songwriter
eras.text: After a four-year break, Brill Bruisers became the band's highest-charting album. Then the drummer of fifteen years left, and Dan Bejar, whose songs had always been the band's wild card, sat out a record.

years.h: Brill Bruisers hits No. 13
years.p: A.C. Newman called it a celebration record. It's the New Pornographers' highest US chart placing and their last album on Matador.

years.h: Kurt Dahle leaves; Joe Seiders takes over drums
years.p: Kurt Dahle, drummer since 1999, leaves mid-2014 and Joe Seiders replaces him.

q: Sometimes we avoided Destroyer, sometimes Destroyer avoided us.
years.h: Whiteout Conditions, the first album without Dan Bejar
years.p: The New Pornographers' first album on their own Collected Work imprint through Concord has no Bejar songs. A.C. Newman said the clash with a Destroyer record was just timing.

eras.title: Departures, a return and a firing
eras.text: The line-up kept changing: a violinist joined and left, Bejar came back and left again, and a founding keyboardist retired. In 2025 an arrest forced the band to remove a member overnight and rethink its own records.

years.h: In the Morse Code of Brake Lights, with Simi Stone
years.p: Violinist and singer Simi Stone, touring with the band since 2015, becomes a full member for the Concord-era album.

years.h: Dan Bejar returns; Blaine Thurier and Simi Stone leave
years.p: Announcing tours playing whole albums, the band confirms Dan Bejar is back, while keyboardist Blaine Thurier, a founder, and Simi Stone depart.

years.h: Continue as a Guest, on Merge
years.p: The New Pornographers move to Merge. Dan Bejar, called a former and possibly future member, gets a co-writing credit on Really Really Light.

years.h: Drummer Joe Seiders arrested; the band fires him
years.p: Joe Seiders is arrested in California on child pornography charges and the band immediately ends his employment.
years.xp: In November 2025 the band confirmed it would carry on and tour North America in 2026. Charley Drayton overdubbed new drum parts on the tenth album, and A.C. Newman said he wanted to re-record three earlier albums to remove Seiders' drumming.

years.h: The Former Site Of, the tenth album
years.p: Merge releases the New Pornographers' tenth album, led by the single Votive. Josh Wells of [[Destroyer|61604b45-8a91-4e33-a1b6-45d7b1fec4e5]] and [[Black Mountain|4898b9ad-f564-4ff1-9046-b1a16dfd5200]] drums on the tour.
